speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: asked the Minister for Education with regard to the application of the PSLE scoring system to those students exempt from studying Mother Tongue Languages (a) what are the guiding principles to determine which Achievement Level (AL) the student will score; and (b) whether there is an assessment of how the new scoring system will impact students with learning disabilities or special needs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what is the rationale and principle behind according a student an exemption from Mother Tongue Language (MTL) in national exams; and (b) whether this principle aligns with the new PSLE scoring system for MTL exemption.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Today, more than 95% of our students take the Mother Tongue Language (MTL) examination at the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) at either the Standard or Foundation level.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This reflects the centrality of MTL learning in our education system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Learning the MTLs allows us to connect with our communities and draws on our rich ethnic heritage and culture to build our unique Singapore identity.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: At the same time, we recognise that for a small group of students, such as those with special educational needs (SEN) or who have been away from Singapore for prolonged periods, it may be challenging for them to study one of our MTLs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Hence, upon application, we may grant them exemption from MTL.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, there are many students with SEN or who have been away and who still take MTL, notwithstanding the difficulties they encounter.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This group of students will take three examinations at the PSLE – English, Mathematics and Science.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Hence, they will receive only three subject scores on their results slip.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The question then is how to use these scores for posting to the next course of study, given that the vast majority of their peers have a score summed up from all four subjects.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is why for purposes of posting, we assign an MTL score for these students by referencing the MTL scores of other students with similar English, Maths and Science scores, including those offering Foundation MTL.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This basic approach will not change when we move from the T-score system to the new Achievement Level (AL) scoring system in 2021.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Denise Phua asked about the underlying principles of this practice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The new AL scoring system is based on the level of attainment by the student himself and moves us away from the approach of the T-score system where a student has to outperform his peers to register a high score.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, when it comes to secondary school posting, the student still needs to use his PSLE score to compete with other students in order to be admitted into a school of his choice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our treatment of students exempted from MTL is aligned with these principles.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For purposes of deriving AL scores, he was exempted from MTL, so no assessment of his standards took place and he has no score.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But for the purposes of secondary school posting, he needs to be compared with other applicants and so we will assign him an MTL score by referencing his peers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We can and must strike a balance between competition amongst students and self-mastery, but realistically, we cannot remove competition totally, and it is also not a reflection of the real life that we are preparing students for.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have done this considering the vast majority of students who offer an official MTL either at the Standard or Foundation levels.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This includes a significant number with SEN or those who have returned to Singapore after prolonged periods overseas.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Currently, about 90% of our Returning Singaporean students study an official MTL, with our schools providing support for their language learning.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Seventy percent of students with SEN in mainstream schools also take MTL at PSLE.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As the score range for those taking Foundation MTL is AL6 to AL8, it would be difficult to justify to those offering it why another student who did not sit for the examination could be assigned a higher score.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ms Denise Phua asked about the implications of the new scoring system on course eligibility and school choices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Any student who scores 22 or below will qualify for an Express course.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Under the current T-score system and the new AL scoring system, the outcomes are similar.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our simulations using the most recent PSLE results show that a similar proportion of students with SEN and are exempted from MTL, would qualify for the Express course under both scoring systems.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In any case, by 2024, Express and Normal streams will be phased out.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In terms of school choices, if we held choice patterns constant, about 60% of them would secure their first choice secondary school, under both scoring systems.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For those concerned about the chances of success to be admitted into specific secondary schools, we have, over the past few years, significantly expanded places in the Direct School Admission (DSA) pathway to better recognise talents and achievements across different domains beyond general academic abilities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Schools are also admitting more students with different strengths and backgrounds, including those with SEN.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, we see students with SEN who are talented in Mathematics, Science, sports and performing arts, and admitted via DSA into the schools of their choices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) and schools will support existing MTL-exempt students affected by the new scoring system in their transition by providing advice on their school choices, and to also explore DSA as an option.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We also recognise that our students with SEN put in tremendous effort to cope with their learning.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MOE has increased the resources to help students in Special Education (SPED) schools, and students with SEN in mainstream schools will also benefit from learning support programmes as well as allied educators for learning and behavioural support.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MOE is committed to continue working with schools in providing the support needed to prepare our students for the PSLE changes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Members also asked if we could delay the implementation of the scoring changes for current cohorts or consider an alternative PSLE scoring system for students with SEN.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Those are relevant factors, but we should exercise that judgement during admission mechanisms like the DSA, instead of compromising the consistency and integrity of the assessment and grading system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Fundamentally, we want an education system with multiple pathways and opportunities, so that every child can maximise his or her potential and be placed in good stead for the future.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I totally understand the importance of MTL and that requests and approvals for exemption of Mother Tongue studies must not be taken lightly.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But for students who are medically certified with SEN and, especially those in special schools taking the PSLE, those who are visually impaired, those who are deaf or autistic SPED students, the PSLE score is the main currency by which they are admitted, they have a chance to go to a mainstream secondary school and education.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Cut-off points are still what many secondary mainstream schools use to admit these students unless one is exceptional enough to qualify for DSA.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Hence, there are genuine concerns by the families and parents of these students.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I have two supplementary questions to ask.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: To the layman, the definition of exemption is that it is not conditional and, therefore, there is no excitement of the lower score if you are exempted.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are some who actually fear that the students are further disadvantaged by putting them back into a pool after recognising all the good work that MOE has done for SEN, that we are now putting these students back into the pool to compete with the rest of the others.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second is to do with informed choices.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know these are deep issues and that MOE has done a lot of thinking about this.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But I ask you not to say "no" to me first, but to take the time to consider these several options and let us work together to see what is the best balanced decision for this group.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In fact, I think the Member has reflected the concerns of parents who are genuinely worried about their children, especially those with SEN.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Perhaps, what I can do is put it in perspective and give the reassurance to those parents that even under the new system, their children will be treated fairly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I will take the second question first because Ms Denise Phua asked whether those who are already in-flight might have chosen otherwise if they had known about this, and whether the current system can remain in place for them so that only the new cohorts coming in for primary school will be under the new system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the students with SEN who are exempted and who are taking PSLE in 2021, they, too, as part of that cohort, will need to be posted to a secondary school.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When you post, the posting has to be done in comparison with other students.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, all the students in that cohort will be posted under an AL system and you cannot remain under a T-score system.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is not possible to do comparison or to delay it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And that is the reason why you have to do it together.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But recognising that you have to do it together, then this is the thought process that MOE went through and we hope that the parents will see that this does not actually disadvantage their children.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The first thing to remember is that, actually, more than 95% of our students take MTL.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is 4.5% who are exempted, out of which about 3% includes those who have SEN.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, out of the ones who have SEN in the mainstream schools, as I mentioned earlier, 70% actually do take MTL at PSLE.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the ones who are exempted are actually a very small percentage.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And for the SEN students who take MTL at PSLE, about 40% of them offer Standard MTL and 30% offer Foundation MTL.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there is actually already a very large group of students with SEN who do MTL and they compare together with the others.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, for those who are exempted, I think Ms Denise Phua asked: can an exemption be an exemption?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The exemption is an exemption because if we followed the existing rule, what it would mean is that the student who, for medical reasons or otherwise, if you held very strictly to the rule, it would mean that that student has to take MTL.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And we have given the exemption in recognition of the fact that such students may, because of SEN or for medical reasons, have great difficulty in coping with MTL and, therefore, have been exempted.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, an exemption is given and they do not have to do MTL.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the difficulty comes, as I explained, with posting, because with posting, it is necessary to see how that child compares with other children.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And, if you apply it very strictly, then given that you did not take MTL, the correct score should actually be zero, meaning that you have the worst possible score, and we did not want to do that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And AL6 is actually not a low score.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, do not be mistaken: AL6 is not a low score and it is still possible for these children to be able to get a place in the Express stream.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Receiving an AL6 for the fourth subject does not automatically disqualify a student from accessing a particular course or his first choice secondary school.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, a student obtaining two AL5s and two AL6s will get a PSLE score of 22 and will still be eligible for the Express/Normal (Academic) option band.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, when we did the simulations, they indicate that, by and large, whether under the current system or whether under the new system, a similar proportion of all MTL-exempt students will be able to qualify for Express or the Express/Normal (Academic) option band and that is about 40% of these students.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, by and large, it would not be very different.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Even now, you do have to assign them a score because there are MTL-exempt students today.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think at the end of the day, the key thing for the parents to ask is: some parents may be concerned about their children who do very well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They may get one for English; one for Mathematics; one for Science and then you get six for your MTL.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, for those who are at the margins, when it comes to the choice of a particular school, there is always the DSA option.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And I would ask, at the end of the day, for the parents to work with the teachers to consider what is the best thing for the child because we do want the best pathway, the best option for the child and, especially children with SEN.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That, MOE will certainly not compromise on because we want to make sure that whichever path they take, they have good opportunities in order to be able to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
